mainEntity.name: When do I need to install a dedicated electrical subpanel for my workshop?

acceptedAnswer.text: You need an electrical subpanel if your planned machinery and climate control exceed your existing circuit capacity. Most basic sheds or detached garages have only a single 15-amp or 20-amp shared circuit, which cannot handle simultaneous tool use, dust extraction, air compressors, and an air conditioner. Installing a dedicated 60-amp to 100-amp subpanel provides separate 120V and 240V circuits for heavy equipment while preventing nuisance breaker trips. It also keeps your workshop's electrical draw from straining your main household breaker panel.
acceptedAnswer.description: You need a subpanel if you plan to run 240V equipment, dust collectors, compressors, or a mini-split alongside standard tools without tripping household breakers.
